subject: ACME POC - integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Subject: ACME POC - integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Laura / team

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned heading into the trial:

Summary of the ask:
- ACME wants a 2-week POC to validate Redwood's chat-generation + tool-calling for product support automation (recommendation + ticket creation workflow).
- Scope: 5k messages/day simulation, streaming responses to UI, and a small tool integration to create tickets in ACME's internal ticketing API.

Proposed success criteria (see attached doc for details):
- Latency: p50 < 400ms, p95 < 1.2s for streaming tokens during typical 2-turn flows
- Cost: token cost consistent with estimate in the SOW (<= 35% over run-rate projection)
- Quality: >= 85% accuracy on intent classification and ticket field extraction against our evaluation set
- Stability: zero data leaks, requests honor customer isolation (VPC-friendly) and logs retained per ACME policy

Integration plan (high level):
- Day 0: onboarding + test account + API keys (we'll provision a sandbox API key scoped to POC)
- Day 1: SDK demo + sample integration (Node.js and Python) - streaming example and tool calling flow
- Day 3: ingest ACME prompts/test prompts, run initial evals, tune prompts + tool mappings
- Day 8: load runs + stability, produce final report and handover

Ownership / points of contact:
- Redwood: Marissa (PM, trial coordinator), Vivek (Sales Engineer), Neha (Solutions Eng - integration lead)
- ACME: Laura (Prod), Rajesh (Engineering)

Attachments: acme-poc-success-criteria.docx, acme-integration-checklist.xlsx

Immediate asks for ACME:
1) Confirm the success criteria above (or flag any adjustments)
2) Provide a sandbox ticketing endpoint and any auth details (or let us know if you want Redwood to mock the ticket call)
3) Share a small set (20-30) of sample prompts / tickets and expected fields so Neha can start the extraction evaluation

I'll set up a short kickoff for Thursday 10am PT unless you prefer a different slot.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole

Quick technical notes / questions from engineering:
1) Authentication: we'll provide a scoped API token (Bearer) for the POC. Any recommended rotation or IP allowlist requirements from your side?
2) Streaming: how does Redwood handle partial responses and tool-call triggers? We need a clear example of the streaming + function call contract for our frontend engineers.
3) Tool calling: the ticket creation should accept a small JSON payload; do you support synchronous tool call replies, or is the recommended pattern to emit a ticket creation event and poll a status endpoint?

If you can share a minimal Node example that shows: (a) initiating a streaming completion, (b) detecting a tool call, and (c) invoking the external ticket API from within the same flow, that'd help speed integration.

Thanks -
Rajesh
Senior Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC - integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Rajesh -

Great questions. I put together a short integration checklist and an example flow below. I'll also bring a runnable Node snippet to Thursday's kickoff and push the sample to the shared Drive link.

Short answers:
- Auth: scoped bearer token is fine; we recommend IP allowlist if you want to limit calls to ACME sandbox (optional). No rotation required during a 2-week POC, but we can accept rotated tokens via the Redwood Console if you plan to rotate them.
- Streaming + tool-calls: Redwood streams token deltas to the client. When the model emits a function/tool call token (we support JSON tool-call payloads), the streaming connection includes a function_call event and the full arguments payload. The client can then synchronously call the external API. If you prefer, we can perform the tool call server-side and return the tool response as part of the next model turn. Both patterns are supported.

Example pattern we'll demo (server-side tool call + streaming):
1) Client opens streaming request to Redwood endpoint (/v1/chat/stream) with tool schema registered.
2) Redwood streams partial tokens; when tool call is emitted, Redwood pauses finalization and sends a function_call event payload to the client.
3) Our server receives the function_call payload, invokes ACME ticket API (sync), takes the response (ticket id), then re-injects the ticket id into the conversation as tool result and calls Redwood to continue generation.

We'll attach a minimal Node.js example (express) showing:
- /start-stream: opens streaming connection
- on function_call: call POST https://sandbox-acme-ticket.acme.com/tickets with provided JSON, return ticket id
- continue generation call with tool result

Files I'll bring: redwood-sdk-sample.zip (Node + Python), acme-integration-checklist.xlsx

- Redwood to provide the Node streaming + tool-call example and a test harness (Neha)
- Marissa to schedule kickoff and share participant Zoom link (Marissa)

Cheers,
